standard_prerequisites: The delta-dimension of a closed subset as the supremum of the delta-dimensions of its irreducible components, and the delta-dimension of a point
Openness of a flat morphism that is locally of finite presentation, and the criterion placing generic points in the schematic locus
The dimension formula for the fibre of a morphism at a point, and the definition of a morphism of a given relative dimension
core_obligations: Reduce to the final statement, namely to an integral closed subspace and an irreducible component of its preimage, because the delta-dimension of a closed subset is a supremum over its components
Replace the base by that integral closed subspace and the source by the preimage, so that the morphism is flat of relative dimension r onto an integral base

Use that the morphism is locally of finite presentation to conclude it is open, and deduce that the image of a generic point of an irreducible component of the source is the generic point of the base, so that the component dominates the base
Place those generic points in the schematic loci of the source and of the base, so that the local ring at the generic point of the source has dimension zero

Apply the dimension formula for the fibre at a point to conclude that the transcendence degree of the residue field extension at those generic points is r, which is the required equality of delta-dimensions
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an integral base and an irreducible component of its preimage
Get dominance of the component from the openness of the flat morphism
Move to the schematic locus and apply the fibre dimension formula to read off the delta-dimension shift
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the behaviour of the delta-dimension under flat morphisms of relative dimension r at source lines 1148-1161, label lemma-flat-inverse-image-dimension, whose proof occupies source lines 1163-1191. The proof reduces the statement about an arbitrary closed subset to the case of an irreducible component of the preimage of an integral closed subspace, which is the only case with content, and then does three things: it uses that the morphism is locally of finite presentation to obtain openness and hence dominance of the component over the base, it places the generic points in the schematic loci so that the local ring at the generic point of the source has dimension zero, and it applies the fibre dimension formula to identify the transcendence degree of the residue field extension with r, which is exactly the required shift of delta-dimensions. The counted statement records neither the reduction nor the dimension computation.
